faqs.question: Does my property qualify me for UAE residency?
faqs.answer: Not every property qualifies. Eligibility depends on the property's value, its registration status, and how the title is held — we run a quick check against the current thresholds before you commit to anything further.

faqs.question: How is residency by property different from other routes?
faqs.answer: It doesn't depend on an employer or a trade licence — once approved, your residency stands on the property itself. That makes it the most stable route for an investor who isn't planning to work or run a business in the UAE.

faqs.question: Can I add my family later?
faqs.answer: Yes. Most clients secure their own residency first, then sponsor a spouse and children once their status is active — we can scope both stages from the start if you already know you will want to.

complianceAreas.title: Corporate Tax
complianceAreas.summary: Registration is tied to your trade licence issue date, not the calendar year — the most commonly missed deadline DSD sees.
complianceAreas.description: UAE Corporate Tax applies to most businesses operating under a UAE trade licence, with registration deadlines set relative to the licence's own issue date. A business that has not yet turned a profit still carries the registration obligation.
obligations: Register within the deadline tied to your licence issue date
Assess Qualifying Free Zone Person exemption eligibility, if applicable
File an annual return even in a loss-making year
Retain supporting financial records for the statutory retention period
complianceAreas.notes: Late registration triggers an administrative penalty independent of whether tax was actually owed for the period.

complianceAreas.title: VAT (Value Added Tax)
complianceAreas.summary: Mandatory once taxable supplies cross the federal threshold — voluntary registration is available below it.
complianceAreas.description: VAT registration becomes mandatory once a business's taxable supplies and imports cross the federal threshold over a rolling 12-month period, with voluntary registration available at a lower threshold for businesses that want to reclaim input tax earlier.
obligations: Monitor taxable turnover against the mandatory threshold
Register with the Federal Tax Authority once triggered
File returns on the assigned filing cycle
Retain export evidence for any zero-rated supply
complianceAreas.notes: Input tax must be claimed in the return period the underlying invoice falls into, not a later period of convenience.

complianceAreas.title: Beneficial Ownership (UBO)
complianceAreas.summary: Applies to who actually owns or controls an entity, not just the names on the trade licence.
complianceAreas.description: UBO regulations require most UAE entities to identify and file the individuals who ultimately own or exercise control over them — a distinction that matters most where ownership sits behind holding companies or nominee arrangements.
obligations: Identify individuals meeting the ultimate ownership/control threshold
File the UBO register with the relevant licensing authority
Maintain a register of nominee directors/managers, if any
Update the filing whenever ownership or control changes
complianceAreas.notes: A correct filing at incorporation does not remain correct automatically — a later ownership change carries its own update obligation.

complianceAreas.title: AML/KYC Compliance
complianceAreas.summary: Applies to Designated Non-Financial Businesses and Professions, not only banks and exchange houses.
complianceAreas.description: Businesses in specified regulated activities — including real estate brokers, precious metals dealers, and certain corporate service providers — carry anti-money-laundering obligations: a written policy, client due diligence, and suspicious-activity reporting through goAML.
obligations: Assess whether your activity falls within a regulated DNFBP category
Adopt a written AML/CFT policy
Perform client due diligence before onboarding
Register and report through the goAML platform
complianceAreas.notes: Obligations apply from the point an activity is regulated, regardless of transaction volume in any given period.

complianceAreas.title: Trade Licence Renewal
complianceAreas.summary: An expired licence affects immigration and banking standing, not just the ability to trade.
complianceAreas.description: Trade licences are issued on an annual cycle and must be renewed before expiry to remain valid — an expired licence can also affect an entity's establishment card and, by extension, its employees' visa status.
obligations: Track the licence expiry date ahead of the renewal window
Settle any outstanding fines before renewal is accepted
Renew the associated establishment/immigration card in step
File any activity or shareholder amendment alongside renewal, if applicable
complianceAreas.sourceName: Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism

complianceAreas.title: Annual Accounting & Bookkeeping
complianceAreas.summary: Books are now a Corporate Tax input, not just a year-end formality.
complianceAreas.description: Since Corporate Tax filing depends on accurate annual financial statements, bookkeeping errors carried through the year now surface directly in a business's tax return — not just its own management reporting.
obligations: Maintain monthly bookkeeping records
Reconcile bank statements against the general ledger
Prepare annual financial statements
Retain records for the statutory retention period

complianceAreas.title: Corporate Governance
complianceAreas.summary: The record-keeping and structural discipline most non-compliance actually traces back to — not a one-time filing.
complianceAreas.description: Corporate governance covers the constitutional records, resolutions, and ownership documentation every UAE company must keep current — memorandum and articles of association, shareholder registers, resolutions, and signing authority. DSD sees the same governance gaps recur across founders: missed renewal deadlines, informal ownership changes, and undocumented management authority that only surface during a bank review or licence renewal.
obligations: Maintain a structured compliance calendar covering trade-licence, tax, and permit renewal deadlines
Keep constitutional documents, shareholder registers, and resolutions accurate and current
Update beneficial-ownership records whenever shareholders, directors, or managers change
Retain accounting records at the company's headquarters for at least five years
Ensure only properly authorised signatories operate bank accounts and sign contracts
Coordinate licence, immigration, and residency renewals rather than treating them separately
complianceAreas.notes: Founders most often lose control of compliance not through one large mistake but by treating governance as administrative overhead rather than a risk-management function that protects the company's licence, banking relationships, and reputation.

complianceAreas.title: Corporate Compliance
complianceAreas.summary: The umbrella obligation — keeping your licence, records, and structure aligned with what's actually true about your company.
complianceAreas.description: Corporate compliance is the ongoing discipline of keeping a company's trade licence, constitutional records, and operational activities aligned with what's actually true — not a single filing, but a continuous standard every UAE company is held to.
obligations: Operate only within your trade licence's approved activities
Keep constitutional documents and shareholder records current
Notify the licensing authority when ownership, management, or address changes
Maintain accurate signing-authority records for contracts and bank accounts
complianceAreas.notes: Compliance is assessed against your company's actual activity, not just what's on file — an outdated licence or record is treated the same as a wrong one.

complianceAreas.title: Accounting & Reporting
complianceAreas.summary: Bookkeeping and financial statements accurate enough to support tax filings, audits, and bank due diligence.
complianceAreas.description: Every UAE company needs financial records reliable enough to support its own tax filings — not reconstructed after the fact. DSD keeps bookkeeping current and produces financial statements that hold up under audit, financing, or bank scrutiny.
obligations: Maintain complete, current bookkeeping — not reconstructed after the fact
Keep personal and company funds clearly separated
Retain invoices and supporting records for the statutory retention period
Prepare financial statements accurate enough to support an external audit
complianceAreas.notes: Banks and free-zone authorities alike increasingly expect financial statements as a matter of course, not only at renewal time.

complianceAreas.title: Tax Compliance
complianceAreas.summary: Corporate Tax and VAT obligations that apply from registration through filing — even in a loss-making year.
complianceAreas.description: UAE Corporate Tax and VAT carry registration and filing obligations independent of whether tax is ultimately owed — a business that hasn't turned a profit yet still has to register and file. DSD tracks both regimes against your specific licence date and turnover.
obligations: Register for Corporate Tax within the deadline tied to your licence issue date
File an annual Corporate Tax return even in a loss-making year
Monitor VAT-taxable turnover against the mandatory registration threshold
File VAT returns on the assigned cycle and retain supporting invoices
complianceAreas.notes: Late registration triggers an administrative penalty independent of whether tax was actually owed for the period.

complianceAreas.title: AML / KYC
complianceAreas.summary: Customer due diligence, screening, and reporting obligations for businesses captured under DNFBP rules.
complianceAreas.description: AML/KYC obligations apply in full force to certain regulated businesses, and DSD determines whether your licensed activity brings you within scope — then builds the customer due diligence, screening, and reporting practice that scope requires.
obligations: Determine whether your licensed activity falls under DNFBP obligations
Verify client and beneficial-owner identity before onboarding
Screen clients against applicable sanctions and PEP lists
Register on the goAML portal and report suspicious activity where required
complianceAreas.notes: AML obligations are actively enforced against corporate service providers specifically, not just banks and financial institutions.
complianceAreas.sourceName: UAE Ministry of Economy and Tourism

complianceAreas.title: Regulatory Support
complianceAreas.summary: Sector-specific approvals and regulator relationships beyond the standard trade licence.
complianceAreas.description: Some activities need approval from a regulator beyond the standard trade licence — healthcare, financial services, and transport among them. DSD identifies which additional approvals your activity actually requires and manages the relationship with that regulator.
obligations: Identify whether your activity requires a sector-specific regulatory approval
Prepare and submit the additional approval application
Maintain the qualifications, premises, or insurance the regulator requires
Track renewal cycles for every regulatory approval held, not just the trade licence
complianceAreas.notes: A general trade licence does not substitute for a required sector-specific approval — operating without one carries its own penalty, independent of the licence itself.
complianceAreas.sourceName: UAE Ministry of Economy and Tourism

complianceAreas.title: Annual Compliance
complianceAreas.summary: The recurring calendar of renewals, filings, and reviews every UAE company runs every year.
complianceAreas.description: Beyond any single obligation, every UAE company works against a recurring annual calendar — licence renewal, tax filings, UBO review, and financial statement preparation, each on its own cycle. DSD maintains that calendar so nothing is left to memory.
obligations: Renew your trade licence before its annual expiry
File Corporate Tax and VAT returns on their respective cycles
Review and update beneficial-ownership records annually
Prepare annual financial statements, audited where required
complianceAreas.notes: Most compliance failures trace back to a missed calendar date, not a misunderstood rule.

insights.title: UAE Golden Visa Through Property: What Qualifies in 2026
insights.summary: A plain breakdown of the property investment thresholds and title-deed requirements behind the 10-year Golden Visa route.
body: Property-based residency is one of the most direct routes into the UAE for investors who already know where they want to buy. The core requirement is a minimum property value, held in the investor's own name, with the title deed registered before the visa application is submitted.

Off-plan property is treated differently to completed units, and mortgaged property is only eligible once a minimum equity threshold is paid down — this is the single most common reason applications get delayed, so it is worth confirming before an offer is made, not after.
DSD reviews the title deed and payment structure with a client before any application is filed, so the eligibility question is answered in days, not after a rejected submission.

insights.title: Corporate Tax Registration: Deadlines and Late-Filing Penalties
insights.summary: Registration windows are tied to licence issue date, not the calendar year — missing one is the most common avoidable penalty DSD sees.
body: UAE Corporate Tax registration deadlines are set relative to each business's own trade licence issue date, not a single fixed calendar date — which is why so many businesses miss theirs without realising a deadline had passed at all.
A late registration triggers an administrative penalty regardless of whether any tax was actually owed for the period. The registration obligation exists independently of profitability.

This is general guidance, not legal or tax advice — DSD recommends confirming your specific registration window against your trade licence with a compliance specialist before relying on any date mentioned here.

insights.title: Five VAT Filing Mistakes DSD Sees Most Often
insights.summary: From late input-tax claims to misclassified zero-rated exports — the recurring errors that turn a routine filing into a corrected one.
body: The most frequent VAT filing error DSD encounters is claiming input tax in the wrong return period, rather than the period the underlying invoice actually falls into. This alone accounts for a large share of the corrections businesses end up needing to file.

A close second is misclassifying an export as zero-rated without holding the export evidence the Federal Tax Authority actually expects to see on request — the classification itself may be correct, but the paper trail behind it is what gets checked.
This is general guidance, not legal or tax advice — treat it as a checklist of things to verify with a compliance specialist, not a substitute for reviewing your own filing.

insights.title: Mainland or Free Zone: How to Actually Decide
insights.summary: The right structure depends on where your clients are, not which jurisdiction has the lower headline fee.
body: The mainland-versus-free-zone decision is usually framed as a cost comparison, but the question that actually determines the right answer is where the business's clients and suppliers are based — a free zone entity trading only with mainland UAE clients adds friction a mainland licence would not.
Free zones remain the simpler route for businesses trading internationally or serving other free zone entities, with 100% foreign ownership and streamlined setup timelines.
DSD scopes this against the client's actual first-year trading plan, not a generic recommendation, before proposing a structure.

insights.title: UBO Filing: What Changed in 2026
insights.summary: An update to the beneficial ownership disclosure requirements that most existing entities still haven't acted on.
body: Beneficial ownership disclosure requirements apply to the individuals who ultimately own or control an entity, not only the names listed on the trade licence — a distinction that matters most for entities with layered or multi-jurisdiction ownership structures.
An entity that filed correctly at incorporation still has an ongoing obligation to update its UBO register whenever ownership or control actually changes, not just at renewal.
This is general guidance, not legal or tax advice — DSD reviews an entity's actual ownership structure against the current filing requirement rather than relying on what was filed at setup.

insights.title: Sponsoring Family Members: Income Thresholds and Housing Rules
insights.summary: The income and accommodation requirements behind a spouse, child, or parent sponsorship application, explained plainly.
body: Family sponsorship eligibility is assessed against the sponsor's own residency status, minimum income, and the accommodation registered under their name — a tenancy contract in someone else's name is the most common reason an otherwise-eligible application stalls.
Sponsoring a parent carries its own, stricter income threshold on top of the standard family requirements, and is assessed separately from a spouse or child application.
DSD checks the sponsor's documentation against the current thresholds before submission, so gaps are caught before they cost an application cycle.
